what: Twilio sells communications as software. Developers use its interfaces to send text messages, emails, WhatsApp messages and phone calls from inside their own applications: the delivery notifications, verification codes and alerts people receive every day.
customers: Software developers and companies of all sizes building customer communications into their products.
money: messaging, voice, email and verification, priced per message
moat: Carrier relationships and deliverability built over fifteen years, plus code written into customers' applications that is tedious to replace.
risks: Gross margin of 49% is low for software because carrier fees are passed through
Operating margin of 3% leaves little room
Large customers can build directly with carriers at scale
Growth is in the low teens rather than the rates it once had
opportunities: Analysts see about 34% upside from current levels
Verification and AI-driven customer messaging are growing use cases
watch: Dollar-based net expansion rate and gross margin.
